explicacion.ayuda: Every figure in this text comes from your result and the columns appear in the order the model weighed them. It is a check of the text, not a guarantee that the model is any good.
explicacion.no_cuadro: The standard text did not match your numbers, so only the figures are shown.

minima.clasificacion: {metric}: the model scores {modelo} and the baseline {base}. The columns that weigh most: {lista}.
minima.numerica: {metric}: the model’s error is {modelo} and the baseline’s {base}. The columns that weigh most: {lista}.

grupos.separan: The groups are told apart mostly by {lista}.
grupos.sin_separan: No column clearly separates the groups.
grupos.sin_rasgos: it looks like the average on the columns that separate most

intervalo.titulo: Margin of error of the figure
intervalo.detalle: The {n} test rows were resampled {remuestreos} times, with seed {semilla}. It is how much the figure would change if the test had been another sample of the same rows; it does not include training on other rows or a change in your data (that is what “Stress it” is for).
intervalo.pocas: With only {n} test rows the interval is very wide: the figure says little.
intervalo.error: The margin of error could not be computed. Train again to try once more.
intervalo.sin_prueba: An imported model does not carry the test it was measured on: the margin of error is computed in the run where you trained it.
intervalo.no_aplica: Clustering has no target and no test: there is no figure with a margin of error to measure.
